mission: Design and, where possible within isolated scope, prepare a canary that proves Context Fabric is actually used rather than merely documented. Require L0/L1/L2 context receipts, compare selected sources against a gold/reference set, test stale/authority/contradiction omission, and measure files/tokens opened versus repository scan.
acceptance_criteria: L0/L1/L2 receipt contract tested against omissions
efficiency metric compares selected context with repo scan
planned_checkpoints: load exact read_scope and persist context receipt
derive gold/reference source set and receipt schema
define efficiency measurement and promotion gate
persist evidence-backed RETURN and mark DONE

context_receipt.mission: Prove actual Context Fabric use via auditable L0/L1/L2 selection, gold-set comparison, omission/freshness/authority/contradiction tests and efficiency measurement.
context_receipt.omission_reason: Not required to derive the narrow Context-Fabric-use canary contract; retained as drill-down refs if a falsifier or dependency requires them.
contradictions_surfaced: PROMETEO_MASTER_CONTEXT_V1 Stage D text is older and says the multi-worker canary is not yet proven, while the current compiled runtime packet reports wave1 evidence with 7 claims, 7 DONE runs and 7 durable returns. The canary must therefore detect stale source conflicts and prefer fresher evidence without erasing the older source.
The public EPOCH changed repeatedly during claim contention and execution, proving that receipts must pin epoch/head rather than merely name files.

budget_estimate.principle: Measure selected evidence against an inventory-derived repository denominator; do not scan the whole repository merely to prove efficiency.

checkpoints_reached: claim won after three safe collision retries
context/acceptance receipt persisted with authority, freshness, contradictions and omissions
efficiency comparison contract defined without fabricated denominator
self-fixture evaluated as PARTIAL_EXPECTED_FAILURE rather than promoted
